newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Brazilian peacekeeper killed in Angolan ambush.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian peacekeeper killed in Angolan ambush.

text.p: A Brazilian peacekeeper in Angola was killed and another wounded by unknown attackers in an ambush in the central rebel-held town of Vila Nova, a United Nations official said on Tuesday.
"One of the peacekeepers was killed and one was injured, a U.N. military official told Reuters.
The official said the peacekeepers, driving a U.N.-marked car, were escorting a civilian vehicle when they were ambushed by bandits on a road near Vila Nova.
Several thousand UNITA troops are assembled at a camp near Vila Nova awaiting demobilisation.
Angolan state television reported that nine civilians were hurt in the attack.

Although the Angolan government and UNITA are partners in a power-sharing government, after the implementation of a two-year peace plan to end 20 years of civil war, many areas are still held by the factions.
The formal handover of rebel territory began three weeks ago in northwestern Angola and was scheduled to continue in Vila Nova this week, although the plans have been postponed by UNITA.
Journalists visiting Vila Nova last week reported that local UNITA commanders have expressed unhappiness over the extension of state administration to the area.

At the northern town of M'banza Congo, the first UNITA town to be handed to the government, aid workers said armed UNITA troops had re-entered the city and had taken down the Angolan flag and replaced it with a UNITA flag.
